Let \(z=(1,x_1,x_2)^T\) and \(\theta=(\beta_0,\beta_1,\beta_2)^T\).

Because the actual R data-generation code, including \(n,n_1\), test-set size, and object names, is not included in the prompt, the numerical values in parts 2 and 5 cannot be uniquely recovered from the distributional description alone. Below I give the exact mathematical answers and reproducible R code which, when run after the supplied data-generation code, prints the requested numerical reports and plot.

---

## 1. Why the logistic model is misspecified

The true conditional log-odds are

\[
\log\frac{P(Y=1\mid X=x)}{P(Y=0\mid X=x)}
=
\log\frac{f_1(x)}{f_0(x)}
\]

because \(P(Y=1)=P(Y=0)=1/2\). Here

\[
\mu_0=(-6,-6)^T,\qquad 
\Sigma_0=\operatorname{diag}(5^2,15^2),
\]

\[
\mu_1=(6,6)^T,\qquad 
\Sigma_1=\operatorname{diag}(5^2,10^2).
\]

Thus

\[
\log\frac{f_1(x)}{f_0(x)}
=
\frac12\log\frac{|\Sigma_0|}{|\Sigma_1|}
-\frac12\left\{(x-\mu_1)^T\Sigma_1^{-1}(x-\mu_1)
-(x-\mu_0)^T\Sigma_0^{-1}(x-\mu_0)\right\}.
\]

Since

\[
|\Sigma_0|=25\cdot 225=5625,\qquad
|\Sigma_1|=25\cdot 100=2500,
\]

we get

\[
\frac12\log\frac{|\Sigma_0|}{|\Sigma_1|}
=
\frac12\log\frac{5625}{2500}
=
\log\frac32.
\]

Expanding the quadratic terms,

\[
\log\frac{P(Y=1\mid X=x)}{P(Y=0\mid X=x)}
=
\log\frac32-\frac{1}{10}
+\frac{12}{25}x_1
+\frac{13}{150}x_2
-\frac{1}{360}x_2^2.
\]

The true log-odds contain the quadratic term \(-x_2^2/360\). The fitted logistic model assumes

\[
\log\frac{P(Y=1\mid X=x)}{P(Y=0\mid X=x)}
=
\beta_0+\beta_1x_1+\beta_2x_2,
\]

which is affine in \(x\). Therefore the logistic model is misspecified.

Equivalently: the class-conditional covariances are unequal, so the Bayes rule is quadratic rather than linear.

---

## 2. Labeled-data MLE and test performance

The labeled MLE solves the usual logistic score equation

\[
0
=
\frac1{n_1}\sum_{i=1}^{n_1}
\{Y_i-\pi(X_i;\theta)\}z_i,
\]

where

\[
\pi(x;\theta)=\frac{\exp(z^T\theta)}{1+\exp(z^T\theta)}.
\]

The following R code reports \((\hat\beta_0,\hat\beta_1,\hat\beta_2)\), average test log-likelihood, and test accuracy. Replace `xs.test, ys.test` by the names used in the supplied code if different.

```r
softplus <- function(t) {
  pmax(t, 0) + log1p(exp(-abs(t)))
}

test_metrics <- function(theta, x, y) {
  z <- cbind(1, as.matrix(x))
  eta <- drop(z %*% theta)
  avg_loglik <- mean(y * eta - softplus(eta))
  acc <- mean((eta >= 0) == (y == 1))
  c(avg_test_loglik = avg_loglik, test_accuracy = acc)
}

## labeled-data logistic MLE
dat.labeled <- data.frame(
  y  = ys[1:n1],
  x1 = xs[1:n1, 1],
  x2 = xs[1:n1, 2]
)

fit.hat <- glm(y ~ x1 + x2, data = dat.labeled, family = binomial())
theta.hat <- unname(coef(fit.hat))
names(theta.hat) <- c("beta0", "beta1", "beta2")

theta.hat
test_metrics(theta.hat, xs.test, ys.test)
```

---

## 3. Loss minimized by \((\tilde\beta_0,\tilde\beta)\)

The semi-supervised estimator is defined by

\[
0
=
\frac1{n_1}\sum_{i=1}^{n_1}Y_i z_i
-
\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n \pi(X_i;\theta)z_i.
\]

Equivalently,

\[
0
=
\nabla_\theta L_n(\theta),
\]

where

\[
L_n(\theta)
=
\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n \log\left\{1+\exp(z_i^T\theta)\right\}
-
\frac1{n_1}\sum_{i=1}^{n_1} Y_i z_i^T\theta.
\]

Indeed,

\[
\nabla_\theta L_n(\theta)
=
\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n \pi(X_i;\theta)z_i
-
\frac1{n_1}\sum_{i=1}^{n_1}Y_i z_i.
\]

Therefore the estimating equation is exactly \(\nabla_\theta L_n(\theta)=0\).

The Hessian is

\[
\nabla_\theta^2 L_n(\theta)
=
\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n
\pi(X_i;\theta)\{1-\pi(X_i;\theta)\}z_i z_i^T,
\]

which is positive semidefinite. Hence \(L_n\) is convex, and any solution of the estimating equation is a global minimizer. If the design matrix has full column rank, the Hessian is positive definite for finite \(\theta\), giving uniqueness.

---

## 4. Newton-Raphson function for \((\tilde\beta_0,\tilde\beta)\)

```r
ssl_newton <- function(xs, ys, n1, start = NULL,
                       tol = 1e-10, maxit = 100, trace = FALSE) {
  x <- as.matrix(xs)
  n <- nrow(x)
  z <- cbind(1, x)
  p <- ncol(z)

  y.labeled <- ys[1:n1]

  ## a = n1^{-1} sum_{i <= n1} Y_i z_i
  a <- drop(crossprod(z[1:n1, , drop = FALSE], y.labeled)) / n1

  loss <- function(theta) {
    eta <- drop(z %*% theta)
    mean(softplus(eta)) -
      sum(y.labeled * eta[1:n1]) / n1
  }

  if (is.null(start)) {
    start <- rep(0, p)
  }

  theta <- as.numeric(start)
  conv <- FALSE

  for (iter in seq_len(maxit)) {
    eta <- drop(z %*% theta)
    prob <- plogis(eta)

    grad <- drop(crossprod(z, prob)) / n - a

    if (max(abs(grad)) < tol) {
      conv <- TRUE
      break
    }

    w <- prob * (1 - prob)
    hess <- crossprod(z, z * w) / n

    step <- tryCatch(
      solve(hess, grad),
      error = function(e) qr.solve(hess, grad)
    )

    oldval <- loss(theta)
    lambda <- 1

    ## Step-halving to ensure descent
    repeat {
      theta.new <- theta - lambda * step
      newval <- loss(theta.new)

      if (is.finite(newval) &&
          newval <= oldval - 1e-4 * lambda * sum(grad * step)) {
        break
      }

      lambda <- lambda / 2
      if (lambda < 1e-8) break
    }

    if (trace) {
      cat(iter,
          "loss =", newval,
          "maxgrad =", max(abs(grad)),
          "lambda =", lambda, "\n")
    }

    if (max(abs(theta.new - theta)) <
        tol * (1 + max(abs(theta)))) {
      theta <- theta.new
      conv <- TRUE
      break
    }

    theta <- theta.new
  }

  eta <- drop(z %*% theta)
  prob <- plogis(eta)
  grad <- drop(crossprod(z, prob)) / n - a

  names(theta) <- c("beta0", "beta1", "beta2")

  list(
    coefficients = theta,
    loss = loss(theta),
    gradient = grad,
    iterations = iter,
    converged = conv
  )
}
```

---

## 5. Semi-supervised estimator and test performance

Run:

```r
fit.tilde <- ssl_newton(xs, ys, n1, start = theta.hat)
theta.tilde <- fit.tilde$coefficients

theta.tilde
test_metrics(theta.tilde, xs.test, ys.test)
```

To print all relevant quantities together:

```r
report <- rbind(
  labeled = c(theta.hat,
              test_metrics(theta.hat, xs.test, ys.test)),
  semisupervised = c(theta.tilde,
                     test_metrics(theta.tilde, xs.test, ys.test))
)

round(report, 6)
```

This gives the requested \((\tilde\beta_0,\tilde\beta_1,\tilde\beta_2)\), average test log-likelihood, and classification accuracy.

---

## 6. Plot training data and three classification lines

The classification line for coefficient vector \(\theta=(\theta_0,\theta_1,\theta_2)\) is

\[
\theta_0+\theta_1x_1+\theta_2x_2=0.
\]

Equivalently, if \(\theta_2\neq 0\),

\[
x_2
=
-\frac{\theta_0}{\theta_2}
-\frac{\theta_1}{\theta_2}x_1.
\]

The full-data MLE using all labels is computed only for comparison:

```r
dat.all <- data.frame(
  y  = ys,
  x1 = xs[, 1],
  x2 = xs[, 2]
)

fit.all <- glm(y ~ x1 + x2, data = dat.all, family = binomial())
theta.all <- unname(coef(fit.all))
names(theta.all) <- c("beta0", "beta1", "beta2")
```

Plot:

```r
cols <- rep("grey70", nrow(xs))
pchs <- rep(1, nrow(xs))

cols[1:n1] <- ifelse(ys[1:n1] == 1, "tomato", "royalblue")
pchs[1:n1] <- 19

plot(xs[, 1], xs[, 2],
     col = cols, pch = pchs,
     xlab = expression(x[1]),
     ylab = expression(x[2]),
     main = "Labeled and unlabeled training data with classification lines")

draw_line <- function(theta, col, lty) {
  if (abs(theta[3]) > 1e-12) {
    abline(a = -theta[1] / theta[3],
           b = -theta[2] / theta[3],
           col = col, lwd = 2, lty = lty)
  } else {
    abline(v = -theta[1] / theta[2],
           col = col, lwd = 2, lty = lty)
  }
}

draw_line(theta.hat,   col = "black",     lty = 1)
draw_line(theta.tilde, col = "darkgreen", lty = 2)
draw_line(theta.all,   col = "purple",    lty = 3)

legend("topright",
       legend = c("labeled Y=0", "labeled Y=1", "unlabeled",
                  "labeled MLE", "semi-supervised", "all-label MLE"),
       col = c("royalblue", "tomato", "grey70",
               "black", "darkgreen", "purple"),
       pch = c(19, 19, 1, NA, NA, NA),
       lty = c(NA, NA, NA, 1, 2, 3),
       lwd = c(NA, NA, NA, 2, 2, 2),
       bty = "n")
```

The three plotted boundaries correspond to

\[
\hat\theta_0+\hat\theta_1x_1+\hat\theta_2x_2=0,
\]

\[
\tilde\theta_0+\tilde\theta_1x_1+\tilde\theta_2x_2=0,
\]

and

\[
\theta_{\text{all},0}+\theta_{\text{all},1}x_1+\theta_{\text{all},2}x_2=0.
\]

  x <- as.matrix(xs)
  n <- nrow(x)
  z <- cbind(1, x)
  p <- ncol(z)

  y.labeled <- ys[1:n1]

  ## a = n1^{-1} sum_{i <= n1} Y_i z_i
  a <- drop(crossprod(z[1:n1, , drop = FALSE], y.labeled)) / n1

  loss <- function(theta) {
    eta <- drop(z %*% theta)
    mean(softplus(eta)) -
      sum(y.labeled * eta[1:n1]) / n1
  }

  if (is.null(start)) {
    start <- rep(0, p)
  }

  theta <- as.numeric(start)
  conv <- FALSE

  for (iter in seq_len(maxit)) {
    eta <- drop(z %*% theta)
    prob <- plogis(eta)

    grad <- drop(crossprod(z, prob)) / n - a

    if (max(abs(grad)) < tol) {
      conv <- TRUE
      break
    }

    w <- prob * (1 - prob)
    hess <- crossprod(z, z * w) / n

    step <- tryCatch(
      solve(hess, grad),
      error = function(e) qr.solve(hess, grad)
    )

    oldval <- loss(theta)
    lambda <- 1

    ## Step-halving to ensure descent
    repeat {
      theta.new <- theta - lambda * step
      newval <- loss(theta.new)

      if (is.finite(newval) &&
          newval <= oldval - 1e-4 * lambda * sum(grad * step)) {
        break
      }

      lambda <- lambda / 2
      if (lambda < 1e-8) break
    }

    if (trace) {
      cat(iter,
          "loss =", newval,
          "maxgrad =", max(abs(grad)),
          "lambda =", lambda, "\n")
    }

    if (max(abs(theta.new - theta)) <
        tol * (1 + max(abs(theta)))) {
      theta <- theta.new
      conv <- TRUE
      break
    }

    theta <- theta.new
  }

  eta <- drop(z %*% theta)
  prob <- plogis(eta)
  grad <- drop(crossprod(z, prob)) / n - a

  names(theta) <- c("beta0", "beta1", "beta2")

  list(
    coefficients = theta,
    loss = loss(theta),
    gradient = grad,
    iterations = iter,
    converged = conv
  )
}
```

## 6. Plot training data and three classification lines

The classification line for coefficient vector \(\theta=(\theta_0,\theta_1,\theta_2)\) is

\[
\theta_0+\theta_1x_1+\theta_2x_2=0.
\]

Equivalently, if \(\theta_2\neq 0\),

\[
x_2
=
-\frac{\theta_0}{\theta_2}
-\frac{\theta_1}{\theta_2}x_1.
\]

The full-data MLE using all labels is computed only for comparison:

```r
dat.all <- data.frame(
  y  = ys,
  x1 = xs[, 1],
  x2 = xs[, 2]
)

fit.all <- glm(y ~ x1 + x2, data = dat.all, family = binomial())
theta.all <- unname(coef(fit.all))
names(theta.all) <- c("beta0", "beta1", "beta2")
```

Plot:

```r
cols <- rep("grey70", nrow(xs))
pchs <- rep(1, nrow(xs))

cols[1:n1] <- ifelse(ys[1:n1] == 1, "tomato", "royalblue")
pchs[1:n1] <- 19

plot(xs[, 1], xs[, 2],
     col = cols, pch = pchs,
     xlab = expression(x[1]),
     ylab = expression(x[2]),
     main = "Labeled and unlabeled training data with classification lines")

draw_line <- function(theta, col, lty) {
  if (abs(theta[3]) > 1e-12) {
    abline(a = -theta[1] / theta[3],
           b = -theta[2] / theta[3],
           col = col, lwd = 2, lty = lty)
  } else {
    abline(v = -theta[1] / theta[2],
           col = col, lwd = 2, lty = lty)
  }
}

draw_line(theta.hat,   col = "black",     lty = 1)
draw_line(theta.tilde, col = "darkgreen", lty = 2)
draw_line(theta.all,   col = "purple",    lty = 3)

legend("topright",
       legend = c("labeled Y=0", "labeled Y=1", "unlabeled",
                  "labeled MLE", "semi-supervised", "all-label MLE"),
       col = c("royalblue", "tomato", "grey70",
               "black", "darkgreen", "purple"),
       pch = c(19, 19, 1, NA, NA, NA),
       lty = c(NA, NA, NA, 1, 2, 3),
       lwd = c(NA, NA, NA, 2, 2, 2),
       bty = "n")
```

The three plotted boundaries correspond to

\[
\hat\theta_0+\hat\theta_1x_1+\hat\theta_2x_2=0,
\]

\[
\tilde\theta_0+\tilde\theta_1x_1+\tilde\theta_2x_2=0,
\]

and

\[
\theta_{\text{all},0}+\theta_{\text{all},1}x_1+\theta_{\text{all},2}x_2=0.
\]
